correctness.rationale: A complete mathematical certificate supplies shattered trees for all n=2..7 at depths 1,2,4,6,9,11, verified by verify.py against every relevant permutation and every root-to-leaf answer path. Cardinality 2^d<=n! closes all n<=6. For n=7, the exact partial-order closure/linear-extension dynamic program in poset_upper.py exhaustively disproves a depth-eleven continuation after any first comparison (16,587 states); an independent concept-bitset recursion in verify_bitset_upper.py gives depth eleven but not twelve (74,797 states). Proof explains why both algorithms are exhaustive, exact, and sound, and provides unrestricted forest-VC and concatenation lemmas. n=1 is the singleton base case. Finite enumeration makes no assertion for n>=8.

originality.rationale: The prior general finite-poset comparison-VC classification already entails the static n-1 dimension, and no novelty is claimed for it. The new adaptive claims are the exact 1..7 Littlestone table, the first deficit relative to floor(log2 n!) at seven, and the disjoint-block amplification lower bound. Actual semantic research-index queries, the accessible previous comparison claim, and relevant published mathematical literature were compared on these statements and implication directions. The inspected 2017 top-k noisy-ranking section and the 2026 ranking-counterexample paper have different feedback and objectives. General Littlestone-theory abstracts and closure bounds do not themselves imply an exact seven-item table. Residual historical-priority uncertainty remains explicit.
residual_risks: Older sorting-decision-tree and teaching-dimension literature may express the maximal complete pair-comparison mistake depth without using Littlestone terminology; historical priority is not conclusively settled.
The full manuscripts of general learning-dimension papers were not all available for inspection; abstract-only conclusions are not used as claims of whole-document noncoverage.
Semantic index search nonappearance does not prove uniqueness or absence of equivalent corollaries.

value.rationale: The first failure at seven of the natural entropy ceiling is a sharp structural boundary in the optimal adversarial online mistake problem for ordering all labels. The exact short table is not an arbitrary parameter slice: it settles the first capacity obstruction beyond cardinality. The complete negative finite proof and explicit positive witnesses provide reusable benchmark instances for adaptive comparison decision-tree complexity. The six-item witness grafts to full unrestricted total-order classes on arbitrarily many labels, proving a linear adaptive-minus-VC gap. This is a mathematical distinction not supplied by the earlier static comparison-support theorem.
